title: CTS Practical Theology — Unit 6: The Word of God in Daily Life

blocks.en: 🌱 Practical Theology — Unit 6: The Word of God in Daily Life
blocks.es_reference: 🌱 Teología Práctica — Unidad 6: La Palabra de Dios en la Vida Diaria

blocks.en: Professors: Dr. Wayne Cook & Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesores: Dr. Wayne Cook y Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: Introduction: A Life Built on the Word
blocks.es_reference: Introducción: Una Vida Edificada sobre la Palabra

blocks.en: We have learned to walk with God, to keep a daily time with Him, and to pray. At the center of all of these stands the Word of God. The Christian does not live by his own wisdom or by the changing opinions of the world, but by what God has spoken. "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God" (Matthew 4:4, NKJV). In this unit we ask what the Word is to us, how it makes us grow, how to take it into our daily lives, and where it is finally meant to lead us.
blocks.es_reference: Hemos aprendido a andar con Dios, a guardar un tiempo diario con Él, y a orar. En el centro de todas estas cosas está la Palabra de Dios. El cristiano no vive por su propia sabiduría ni por las opiniones cambiantes del mundo, sino por lo que Dios ha hablado. "No sólo de pan vivirá el hombre, sino de toda palabra que sale de la boca de Dios" (Mateo 4:4, RVG). En esta unidad preguntamos qué es la Palabra para nosotros, cómo nos hace crecer, cómo tomarla en nuestra vida diaria, y a dónde está finalmente destinada a llevarnos.

blocks.en: I. The Word Is Our Daily Food
blocks.es_reference: I. La Palabra Es Nuestro Alimento Diario

blocks.en: Scripture again and again compares the Word of God to food, because we need it as truly and as regularly as we need our daily bread. Job said of God, "I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my necessary food" (Job 23:12, NKJV). The prophet Jeremiah said, "Your words were found, and I ate them, and Your word was to me the joy and rejoicing of my heart" (Jeremiah 15:16, NKJV). Peter urges the youngest believers, "as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby" (1 Peter 2:2, NKJV). And this food is living food, for "the word of God is living and powerful, and sharper than any two-edged sword" (Hebrews 4:12, NKJV). A believer who neglects the Word grows weak in the same way a body grows weak that refuses to eat.
blocks.es_reference: La Escritura una y otra vez compara la Palabra de Dios con el alimento, porque la necesitamos tan verdadera y regularmente como necesitamos nuestro pan de cada día. Job dijo de Dios: "guardé las palabras de su boca más que mi comida" (Job 23:12, RVG). El profeta Jeremías dijo: "Fueron halladas tus palabras, y yo las comí; y tu palabra me fue por gozo y por alegría de mi corazón" (Jeremías 15:16, RVG). Pedro exhorta a los creyentes más jóvenes: "desead, como niños recién nacidos, la leche no adulterada de la palabra, para que por ella crezcáis" (1 Pedro 2:2, RVG). Y este alimento es alimento vivo, pues "la palabra de Dios es viva y eficaz, y más penetrante que toda espada de dos filos" (Hebreos 4:12, RVG). El creyente que descuida la Palabra se debilita del mismo modo que se debilita un cuerpo que se niega a comer.

blocks.en: II. How the Word Makes Us Grow
blocks.es_reference: II. Cómo Nos Hace Crecer la Palabra

blocks.en: The last command Peter left us is, "but grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ" (2 Peter 3:18, NKJV). How does a Christian grow? Chiefly by feeding on the Word. There is no growth in grace apart from the steady intake of Scripture, just as there is no growth in a child apart from food. The first Psalm describes the blessed man this way: "his delight is in the law of the Lord, and in His law he meditates day and night. He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that brings forth its fruit in its season" (Psalm 1:2–3, NKJV). Notice the picture: a tree that bears fruit because its roots are sunk deep in a steady supply of water. So it is with the believer who reads, hears, and meditates on the Word regularly — not in fits and starts, but day by day. This is why faithful Bible reading, faithful sitting under the preaching of the Word in the gathered church, and a willingness to sacrifice lesser things for it are among the surest ways a Christian grows.
blocks.es_reference: El último mandato que Pedro nos dejó es: "Mas creced en la gracia y el conocimiento de nuestro Señor y Salvador Jesucristo" (2 Pedro 3:18, RVG). ¿Cómo crece un cristiano? Principalmente alimentándose de la Palabra. No hay crecimiento en la gracia aparte de la constante ingestión de la Escritura, así como no hay crecimiento en un niño aparte del alimento. El primer Salmo describe así al varón bienaventurado: "sino que en la ley de Jehová está su delicia, y en su ley medita de día y de noche. Será como árbol plantado junto a corrientes de aguas, que da su fruto en su tiempo" (Salmos 1:2–3, RVG). Note la imagen: un árbol que da fruto porque sus raíces están hundidas en una provisión constante de agua. Así es con el creyente que lee, oye, y medita en la Palabra regularmente — no a tropezones, sino día tras día. Por eso la lectura fiel de la Biblia, el fiel sentarse bajo la predicación de la Palabra en la iglesia reunida, y la disposición de sacrificar cosas menores por ella, están entre los modos más seguros en que crece un cristiano.

blocks.en: III. Taking the Word In: Read, Meditate, Memorize, Obey
blocks.es_reference: III. Recibir la Palabra: Leer, Meditar, Memorizar, Obedecer

blocks.en: There are four simple ways to take the Word into daily life, and the believer who practices all four will be well fed. First, read it. Have a plan — a portion each day, perhaps a chapter, or a few verses read slowly — so that over time the whole counsel of God passes through your heart. Second, meditate on it. To meditate is not to empty the mind but to fill it: to turn a verse over slowly, as a cow chews its cud, asking what it says about God, about ourselves, and about how we are to live. Third, memorize it. "Your word I have hidden in my heart, that I might not sin against You" (Psalm 119:11, NKJV). A verse carried in the heart is ready in the hour of temptation, when no Bible is open before us. Fourth, and above all, obey it. As we learned in our first unit, we are to be "doers of the word, and not hearers only" (James 1:22, NKJV). Knowledge that is never obeyed puffs up; the Word truly received always bends the life toward obedience.
blocks.es_reference: Hay cuatro maneras sencillas de tomar la Palabra en la vida diaria, y el creyente que practica las cuatro estará bien alimentado. Primero, léala. Tenga un plan — una porción cada día, quizá un capítulo, o unos pocos versículos leídos despacio — para que con el tiempo todo el consejo de Dios pase por su corazón. Segundo, medite en ella. Meditar no es vaciar la mente sino llenarla: dar vuelta a un versículo despacio, como la vaca rumia, preguntando qué dice acerca de Dios, de nosotros mismos, y de cómo hemos de vivir. Tercero, memorícela. "En mi corazón he guardado tus dichos, para no pecar contra ti" (Salmos 119:11, RVG). Un versículo llevado en el corazón está listo en la hora de la tentación, cuando no hay Biblia abierta delante de nosotros. Cuarto, y sobre todo, obedézcala. Como aprendimos en nuestra primera unidad, hemos de ser "hacedores de la palabra, y no tan solamente oidores" (Santiago 1:22, RVG). El conocimiento que nunca se obedece envanece; la Palabra verdaderamente recibida siempre inclina la vida hacia la obediencia.

blocks.en: IV. Where the Word Leads: To Christ Himself
blocks.es_reference: IV. A Dónde Lleva la Palabra: A Cristo Mismo

blocks.en: The written Word is not an end in itself. Its great purpose is to bring us to a Person. The Lord Jesus rebuked those who searched the Scriptures yet missed their point: "You search the Scriptures, for in them you think you have eternal life; and these are they which testify of Me" (John 5:39, NKJV). After His resurrection, "beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, He expounded to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself" (Luke 24:27, NKJV). All Scripture points to Christ, the living Word, of whom John wrote, "the Word became flesh and dwelt among us" (John 1:14, NKJV). So when you open your Bible each day, do not read merely to gather facts or to win arguments; read to meet your Lord, to hear His voice, and to be changed into His likeness. The written Word in our hands is meant to lead us to the living Word, Jesus Christ.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra escrita no es un fin en sí misma. Su gran propósito es traernos a una Persona. El Señor Jesús reprendió a los que escudriñaban las Escrituras y sin embargo erraban su punto: "Escudriñad las Escrituras... ellas son las que dan testimonio de mí" (Juan 5:39, RVG). Después de su resurrección, "comenzando desde Moisés, y de todos los profetas, les declaraba en todas las Escrituras lo que de él decían" (Lucas 24:27, RVG). Toda la Escritura apunta a Cristo, el Verbo vivo, de quien Juan escribió: "Y el Verbo fue hecho carne, y habitó entre nosotros" (Juan 1:14, RVG). Así que cuando abra su Biblia cada día, no lea meramente para reunir datos o para ganar discusiones; lea para encontrarse con su Señor, para oír su voz, y para ser transformado a su semejanza. La Palabra escrita en nuestras manos está destinada a llevarnos al Verbo vivo, Jesucristo.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: The Word of God is our daily food, the means of our growth, and the path that leads us to Christ. To read it, meditate on it, memorize it, and obey it is not a burden laid on us to earn God's favor, but the privilege of children feeding at their Father's table. Make the Word a daily companion, and you will find your walk with God steadied, your prayers deepened, and your life slowly but surely conformed to the Savior of whom every page speaks.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra de Dios es nuestro alimento diario, el medio de nuestro crecimiento, y la senda que nos lleva a Cristo. Leerla, meditar en ella, memorizarla, y obedecerla no es una carga puesta sobre nosotros para ganar el favor de Dios, sino el privilegio de los hijos que se alimentan a la mesa de su Padre. Haga de la Palabra una compañera diaria, y hallará su andar con Dios afirmado, sus oraciones profundizadas, y su vida lenta pero seguramente conformada al Salvador de quien habla cada página.

sa.prompt: According to Matthew 4:4, by what does man truly live, and what does this teach about the Word?
sa.model: According to Matthew 4:4, man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God. This teaches that the Word is as necessary to our spiritual life as food is to our physical life — we cannot truly live, spiritually, without it.

sa.prompt: Give two ways Scripture compares the Word of God to food.
sa.model: Job said he treasured the words of God's mouth more than his necessary food (Job 23:12), and Jeremiah said God's words became to him the joy and rejoicing of his heart when he 'ate' them (Jeremiah 15:16). Peter also urges believers, as newborn babes, to desire the pure milk of the word that they may grow by it (1 Peter 2:2).

sa.prompt: How does the Word of God make a Christian grow (2 Peter 3:18; Psalm 1)?
sa.model: Peter's final command is to grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ (2 Peter 3:18), and this growth comes chiefly by feeding on the Word. Psalm 1 pictures the blessed man who meditates on God's law day and night as a tree planted by rivers of water, bearing fruit because its roots are sunk deep in a steady supply.

sa.prompt: Name the four ways to take the Word into daily life given in this unit.
sa.model: The four ways to take the Word into daily life are: read it, with a regular plan; meditate on it, turning a verse over slowly; memorize it, hiding it in the heart; and, above all, obey it, being a doer of the word and not a hearer only.

sa.prompt: What does it mean to meditate on the Word?
sa.model: To meditate on the Word is not to empty the mind but to fill it — to turn a verse over slowly, the way a cow chews its cud, asking what it says about God, about ourselves, and about how we are to live. It is a slow, reflective dwelling on Scripture, not a quick reading and moving on.

Psalm 119:11 says, 'Your word I have hidden in my heart, that I might not sin against You.' We should memorize Scripture because a verse carried in the heart is ready in the hour of temptation, when no Bible is open before us — it guards us from sin in the very moment we need it most.

sa.prompt: Above all, what must we do with the Word, and what verse teaches this?
sa.model: Above all we must obey the Word, as James 1:22 teaches: 'be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.' Knowledge that is never obeyed puffs up; the Word truly received always bends the life toward obedience, not just toward more information.

sa.prompt: What is the great purpose of the written Word, and where does it lead us?
sa.model: The great purpose of the written Word is not to be an end in itself but to bring us to a Person — Jesus Christ, the living Word. It leads us to meet our Lord, hear His voice, and be changed into His likeness, not merely to gather facts or win arguments.

sa.prompt: How do the Scriptures relate to Christ (John 5:39; Luke 24:27)?
sa.model: Jesus said the Scriptures testify of Him (John 5:39), and after His resurrection He expounded in all the Scriptures, beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, the things concerning Himself (Luke 24:27). All Scripture, then, points to Christ, the living Word who became flesh and dwelt among us.

sa.prompt: Is feeding on the Word a way to earn God's favor, or something else?
sa.model: Feeding on the Word is not a way to earn God's favor; it is the privilege of a child feeding at his Father's table. We are saved by grace through faith as the gift of God, so reading, meditating on, memorizing, and obeying the Word are gifts by which we grow in a relationship already given to us, not payments toward one we must win.
